application_clarification: In A7, R-flatness alone concerns C-scalars and does not establish injectivity of every bounded parameter polynomial on a component. Use the actual generic component dominance proved in A4. Since S is R-flat, S injects into B=S[1/a], which is reduced and has finitely many normal domain components B_i. Let p_i be the contractions of their zero primes. Their intersection in S is0. Any minimal prime p of S contains the finite product of the p_i, hence contains one p_i; minimality forces equality. All minimal primes of S therefore come from generic components. A4 proves T_n injects into each B_i: its kernel, if nonzero, would lower component dimension below n under the finite integral extension. Consequently R_n injects into each S/p_i, and its fraction extension is the corresponding finite generic component field. Apply the explicit normal-base going-down argument A6 to these domain components, then lift the resulting prime back into S. If p is minimal over m_C S, choose a minimal prime p_i contained in p, go down in S/p_i from its contracted q to m_C R_n, and lift p_0 into S. It contains m_C S and lies below p, so minimality forces p_0=p. This proves the desired dimension n without using flatness as a substitute for parameter dominance. Both254 and this addendum remain unreviewed, with no new acceptance or original closure.
